text:
rachel: morning! brand new hire here. followed vpn onboarding but internal hosts like grafana.internal.redwood don't resolve in chrome or dev containers. `ping grafana.internal.redwood` -> unknown host. macbook pro, Ventura, using 'redwood-split'.

it-support: welcome @rachel. quick Q: do you see the corporate DNS server in your resolver list? `scutil --dns` will show.

rachel: scutil shows DNS server 10.51.0.5 for 'utun2' but search domains are empty. when i `dig grafana.internal.redwood @10.51.0.5` i get the A record.

neteng: sounds like split-tunnel isn't pushing the search suffix so unqualified names fail. Chrome/containers won't append the internal.search domain. Two options: use FQDN (grafana.internal.redwood.) or add the search domain locally.

it-support: for Mac, temporary fix: `sudo networksetup -setsearchdomains 'utun2' internal.redwood` but note that networksetup sometimes resets on VPN reconnect.

rachel: tried that — chrome still prefers local DNS cache and some dev containers still can't resolve. any container-friendly workaround?

infra-bot: infra-note: container runtime respects host /etc/resolv.conf on mac via docker-desktop translation; if host resolver uses mDNS or split stub, containers might see 127.0.0.1 which breaks.

neteng: for containers, easiest is to launch with --dns=10.51.0.5 and --add-host entries for baked images. For a quick fix try `docker run --rm --dns 10.51.0.5 busybox nslookup grafana.internal.redwood`.

rachel: that worked! docker resolved when I passed --dns. But i still want non-FQDN to work in terminal. the networksetup trick helps but gets wiped when i sleep the laptop.

it-support: ok we'll add a persistent script to run on network change via a small LaunchAgent. do you want me to push that to your laptop?

rachel: yes please. also, any policy on switching to full-tunnel while onboarding to avoid these fiddly DNS things?

people-ops: if you're doing infra work it's fine to switch to full-tunnel until device enrollment is complete. otherwise keep split to reduce home-latency. we'll mark you on the onboarding list so neteng knows to watch your IP.

ops-bot: Auto-ticket NETWORK-4821 created: push persistent DNS search for onboarding pool (assignee: neteng).

neteng: we'll add a DHCP option for onboarding pool to advertise search domain and submit a small config to avoid stomping by macOS. in the meantime IT will push the LaunchAgent.

it-support: pushed LaunchAgent with id com.redwood.vpn.searchdomains; it will reapply on utun events. can you reboot or just `launchctl load`?

rachel: loaded it, search domain persists after sleep. containers still need --dns for now but terminal lookups work. thanks everyone, saved my first-day debugging time. closing this thread :wave:
